root_cause.text: The ext2_iget() function contained incomplete validation logic that permitted inodes with zero link counts but valid mode and no deletion timestamp to bypass corruption checks and propagate to the VFS layer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies the conditional check in fs/ext2/inode.c to distinguish between deleted inodes (zero mode or set dtime) and corrupted inodes (zero nlink with valid mode and zero dtime), rejecting the latter with -EFSCORRUPTED instead of allowing them to reach namei.c paths where they trigger WARN_ON in drop_nlink().

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement assigns the nlink count from raw_inode directly to the inode without validating that the link count is non-zero when the mode is valid and deletion timestamp is absent. According to the vulnerability root cause, this allows inodes with zero link counts to bypass corruption checks and propagate to the VFS layer. The incomplete validation logic permits this unsafe assignment to occur, making this the critical vulnerable statement that enables the corruption propagation.
